name: Dar-us-Sakina
mission: DAR-US-SAKINA IS A 501(C)(3) NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION DEDICATED TO INCLUSION OF INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES IN THE MUSLIM COMMUNITY OF HOUSTON. OUR PLATFORM IS A SAFE SPACE FOR PEOPLE OF ALL ABILITIES AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. WE INSPIRE THE COMMUNITY TO ABANDON STIGMAS AND EMBRACE INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES WITH EMPATHY AND RESPECT. TOGETHER, WE ARE BETTER.

strengths.detail: Dar-us-Sakina earned <cite id="1">a 93/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting solid board oversight and governance practices.
The organization provides direct localized support, delivering specialized programs for 581 beneficiaries in the Houston area.
Data indicates high fundraising efficiency, spending <cite id="1">just $0.18 per $1 raised</cite> in public contributions.

strengths_deep_dive: Dar-us-Sakina fills a distinct niche within the Houston area by delivering inclusive programs tailored to Muslim individuals with disabilities <cite id="5">including weekend classes and adult day services</cite>. Governance practices are supported by a fully independent board of directors and strong fiscal management, earning <cite id="1">a 93/100 rating on Charity Navigator</cite>. Additionally, the organization demonstrates lean development spending, expending <cite id="1">$0.18 per $1 raised</cite> while maintaining 15.9 months of working capital reserves in FY2024.
rich_narrative.summary: Dar-us-Sakina provides specialized education, adult day programs, and community support for Muslims with disabilities in Houston <cite id="5">through services like Sunday school and adult programs</cite>. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">a total revenue of $1,115,693</cite>, reflecting early-stage growth from its FY2022 revenue of $391,670. The charity maintains <cite id="1">a 93/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>. Its filed program expense ratio of 72.2% in FY2024 falls slightly below the 75% sector benchmark, leaving roughly a quarter of expenditures for administrative and fundraising overhead. The charity delivers direct programming to 581 individuals at a cost of $733.90 per beneficiary, operating within a specialized niche for local families. Donors can support its work through <cite id="2">zakat-eligible contributions</cite> targeting local needy beneficiaries.
